## Proof

Let $Y_i = X_i^2$. Since $X_i \sim U[0,1]$ are i.i.d., the $Y_i$ are i.i.d. nonnegative random variables. We have
$$\frac{D_n^2}{n} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n Y_i.$$

Compute the moments of $Y_i$:
$$\mathbb{E}[Y_i] = \mathbb{E}[X_i^2] = \int_0^1 x^2\,dx = \frac{1}{3},$$
$$\mathbb{E}[Y_i^2] = \mathbb{E}[X_i^4] = \int_0^1 x^4\,dx = \frac{1}{5},$$
$$\operatorname{Var}(Y_i) = \mathbb{E}[Y_i^2] - (\mathbb{E}[Y_i])^2 = \frac{1}{5} - \frac{1}{9} = \frac{4}{45}.$$

Since the $Y_i$ are i.i.d. with finite mean $\mu = 1/3$ and finite, nonzero variance $\sigma^2 = 4/45$, the classical Central Limit Theorem gives
$$\frac{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n Y_i - \mu}{\sigma/\sqrt{n}} \xrightarrow{d} N(0,1),$$
i.e.,
$$Z_n := \frac{D_n^2/n - 1/3}{\sqrt{4/(45n)}} \xrightarrow{d} Z \sim N(0,1).$$

Now observe that
$$F_{D_n/\sqrt{n}}\!\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = \mathbb{P}\!\left(\frac{D_n}{\sqrt{n}} \le \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = \mathbb{P}\!\left(\frac{D_n^2}{n} \le \frac{1}{3}\right) = \mathbb{P}\!\left(\frac{D_n^2}{n} - \frac{1}{3} \le 0\right) = \mathbb{P}(Z_n \le 0).$$

Since $Z_n \xrightarrow{d} Z \sim N(0,1)$ and $0$ is a continuity point of the standard normal CDF $\Phi$, the portmanteau theorem yields
$$\lim_{n\to\infty} \mathbb{P}(Z_n \le 0) = \Phi(0) = \frac{1}{2}.$$

Therefore,
$$\lim_{n\to\infty} F_{D_n/\sqrt{n}}\!\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = \boxed{\frac{1}{2}}.$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
